transcript.text: Our Bosch dryer keeps stopping with the empty water container light on but the container is empty?? We've emptied it like 5 times

This is a very common and frustrating issue with Bosch condenser dryers (and many other brands). If the container is definitely empty, the problem is almost certainly not that the tank is full, but rather that the sensor or switch detecting the water level is stuck, dirty, or blocked.

Here’s a step-by-step guide to troubleshooting and fixing this:

### 1. Check for Physical Obstructions (Most Common)
The water container has a small float or lever inside it that rises with the water level. If lint, debris, or mineral buildup is sticking this mechanism, it will falsely signal "full."
• Remove the container and inspect the float/lever inside the tank. Move it up and down manually. It should move freely without sticking. Clean it thoroughly with warm soapy water and a soft brush (an old toothbrush works well).
• Check the slot in the dryer cabinet where the container slides in. There may be a corresponding sensor or lever there. Ensure it’s clean and moves freely.

### 2. Clean the Condenser Unit
If the condenser is clogged with lint, water can’t drain properly into the tank, causing overflow or sensor errors.
• Remove the condenser unit (usually located at the bottom front).
• Rinse it thoroughly under warm water until the water runs clear.
• Let it dry completely before reinserting.

### 3. Check for Mineral Buildup (Hard Water Areas)
If you live in a hard water area, limescale can coat the sensors and internal pipes, causing false readings.
• Run a cleaning cycle using a dedicated dryer cleaner or a descaling solution designed for Bosch dryers.
• Alternatively, run an empty cycle with a cup of white vinegar in the condenser housing (if your model allows) to help dissolve scale.

### 4. Inspect the Drain Hose (If Applicable)
Some Bosch models can be connected to a drain hose instead of using the container. If you’re using the container but have a drain hose attached:
• Ensure the drain hose isn’t kinked or clogged.
• Some models will still show the "empty container" light if the drain path is blocked, even if the tank is empty.

### 5. Reset the Dryer
Sometimes the electronic control board gets confused.
• Turn off the dryer using the power button.
• Unplug it from the wall for at least 10–15 minutes. This allows the capacitors to discharge and the system to reset.
• Plug it back in and try again.

### 6. Check the Water Level Sensor (Advanced)
If none of the above works, the water level sensor itself may be faulty. This is a small electronic component near the container slot.
• You can test it with a multimeter if you’re comfortable doing so, but this usually requires professional service.
• In many cases, simply cleaning the area around the sensor (as in Step 1) resolves the issue because lint or moisture has caused a short circuit.

### When to Call Bosch Service:
If you’ve cleaned everything thoroughly, reset the unit, and the problem persists, it’s likely a faulty water level sensor or a problem with the main control board. At this point, contact Bosch customer support or a qualified appliance repair technician.

Pro Tip: For future prevention, clean the condenser and lint filter after every few cycles, and descale your dryer every 3–6 months if you have hard water.

I don't have a multimeter, and I can't pull the dryer out because it's stacked on the washer. Anything else I can try?

Since you’ve already done the standard cleaning steps (condenser, filters, container sieve) and the unit is hard to access, let’s focus on the most likely culprits that don’t require disassembly or tools:

### 1. The "Float" Inside the Container
   • Remove the water container completely.
   • Look inside for a small plastic float (usually a white or translucent disc) near the bottom. It should move freely up and down when you tilt the tank. If it’s stuck, clean around it with warm soapy water and a soft brush. Even a tiny bit of lint or slime can cause it to stick in the "up" position, triggering the false "full" signal.

### 2. Sensor Contacts in the Dryer Cavity
   • With the container removed, inspect the slot where the container slides in. There should be two small metal contacts (or a plastic lever) at the bottom or side of the cavity.
   • Wipe these contacts with a dry cloth to remove any dust, lint, or moisture buildup. If they’re corroded or dirty, they may not register the container’s presence correctly.

### 3. Reset the Dryer
   • Unplug the dryer from power for 5–10 minutes. This can reset the electronic control board if it’s glitching. Plug it back in and try a short cycle to see if the error clears.

### 4. Check for Water Residue in the Cavity
   • Even if the container is empty, water might be pooling at the bottom of the dryer cavity where the container sits. Use a dry cloth or paper towel to soak up any moisture there. A damp sensor can trigger false readings.

### 5. Test with a "Fake" Container Weight
   • Sometimes the issue is a faulty switch in the container itself. Try placing a small weight (e.g., a coin) on top of the float inside the empty container to see if it overrides the sensor. If the dryer runs, the container’s internal mechanism is likely broken and needs replacement.

### 6. Hard Water/Scale Buildup
   • If you have hard water, limescale can coat internal sensors or pipes. Run a cleaning cycle with a dedicated dryer descaler (or white vinegar in the condenser housing if your model allows). This may dissolve scale blocking water flow or sensor accuracy.

### 7. Contact Bosch Support
   • Since the dryer is stacked and you can’t access internal components, this may require professional service. Bosch has a reputation for responsive customer support—call them to describe the issue. They may offer troubleshooting tips specific to your model or arrange a technician visit.

### Key Takeaway:
The most likely fix is cleaning the float in the container and resetting the dryer. If these don’t work, the internal sensor or control board may be faulty, requiring professional repair. Given the stacking constraint, Bosch support is your best next step for model-specific guidance.
